Android itself knows which links an app opens (for example, a bank's site). Those sites also bypass the VPN in the browser, just like the app. Works on Android 12 and newer; Telegram, YouTube, Google and similar are never included.

Steam, GitHub, Wikipedia, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, AliExpress, Zoom, Twitch and similar open directly: faster and with less traffic. Telegram, YouTube, Instagram, Discord, ChatGPT, Claude and everything censored in Russia stays in the VPN.

Without these permissions Android (especially MIUI/HyperOS) may not start collection at night while the app is closed. Then collection runs when you first open the phone or the app.
Whitelists: only Russian sites open. Blacklists: individual sites are blocked. Each mode has its own sources, statistics and bypass list. Nightly collection runs for each mode that has sources.

Sometimes the internet is "there" but photos and pages barely load. While you use the phone, every 45 seconds the app checks how much data flows through the server; if it is low, one small test is made (up to 400 KB), and after two slow ones in a row other servers are tried. If the phone is not in use, nothing is downloaded.

The file saves settings and, for each mode (whitelists and blacklists), targets with their check addresses and policy, apps and sites that bypass the VPN, your own sources, the source blocklist, selected services and the accumulated experience of configs (where they worked). Downloaded configs and the log are not included: they are refreshed by the nightly collection. Target servers are not saved either because they contain access keys: after import they will be picked again.

Share is how many configs of the link respond among the checked ones (a fresh check within 7 days or experience on the current network). "High" priority: configs of this link are tried before other live ones, and the link itself is not blocklisted by the audit. "Low": its configs go to the very end of the queue.
If IPv6 is not routed into the tunnel, IPv6 sites open directly, bypassing the VPN (a leak). Blocking makes apps switch to IPv4 over the VPN right away. Applied at the next connection.
If the VPN could not start or dropped, the tunnel stays on and traffic is blocked while the app looks for a working server. Off by default: then on failure the internet goes directly.

If you turn on the "Phoenix: site in browser" accessibility service, the app sees only the domain of the open site (the address bar of Chrome, Yandex, Samsung, Firefox, Opera, Edge, Brave and a few more browsers) and, when switching servers, picks one where that site opens. The domain is kept only in memory, page content is not read, nothing is sent. On Android 13 and newer, for an app not from a store first open "App info" → ⋮ menu → "Allow restricted settings".
If no backup server is found, the app starts a full recheck of all configs by itself (no more than once per 30 minutes).
If the tunnel stops working (three failed checks), the app tries backup configs with the best rating.

Import erases nothing: lists are merged (the source blocklist only grows), targets are added to existing ones, single settings are taken from the file. The file is plain text, you can open and read it. It may contain links to your sources, so do not send it to strangers.
